rules.loss: Wilson 95 % CI on exact loss. Equal: RadiANT upper CI <= reference point + 0.5 pp. Better: RadiANT upper CI < reference lower CI. Worse: RadiANT lower CI > reference point + 0.5 pp.
rules.acquire: Median time to first packet over the cycles. Equal: <= reference median + 0.25 s. Better: lower median AND RadiANT Q3 < reference Q1. Worse: > reference median + 0.25 s.
rules.ladder: 5 %-loss TX power. Equal: within 1 dB (the ab_gates repeatability limit). Better: more than 1 dB lower. Worse: more than 1 dB higher. Inconclusive if either dial check failed or either ladder never reached its knee.
rules.acked: Wilson 95 % CI on the acknowledged-transfer failure rate (sent - completed), the loss rule applied unchanged.
rules.usb: ant_bench round-trip latency. Equal: median <= reference median x 1.1. Better: lower median AND lower p99. Worse: median > reference median x 1.1.

caveats: Every figure is for this fixed placement: antenna and position are part of each result until a swap round separates them.
The Feather transmits from ant_sim.py (EVENT_TX-paced host masters) on its pre-SLIP_GUARD image, at its bridge default power.
A drop is the finding here, not the loss figures; four masters on one board share one clock.
54L15 attach over UART, not USB: excluded from the usb phase, and their receive path includes a UART rather than the USB stack a real dongle has.
RSSI is not comparable across chip families (each reports on its own calibration); it is shown, never judged.

Some loss figures are wall-clock (received radio messages against the window's slot count), not the transmitter's event counter: ant_verify withholds 'loss (exact)' once the counter stands still even once, and the DK master occasionally re-sends its previous buffer when a host refill misses a slot. That repeat lands on every receiver in the window alike, so the receiver-minus-reference gap is unaffected; the absolute figures assume the transmitter's crystal is exact.
